finding: The stated lock window is measured from the owner check, but staleness is measured from acquire, so the rename can land after the lock is stolen
why: _steal_if_stale judges age from the lock folder's mtime, set once when _acquire writes the owner file and never refreshed, so a holder whose _load, write, fsync and own _owner retries (each up to ~2s via _patient) push the check past ~8s can still pass it and then spend up to ~2s in _patient(os.replace) while a second writer steals at 10s, loads the pre-rename manifest and publishes; whichever replace lands last silently drops the other's update, both callers get success, and SDD §7 I10 / Acceptance '2 racing writers lose no update' is broken.
fix: Refresh the lock right before the owner check (os.utime(lock), then compare _owner(lock) to token) so the post-check rename always has the full LOCK_STALE margin, or skip the rename and redo when time since acquire + 2s >= LOCK_STALE; make the comment state the bound the code enforces.
evidence: manifest.py:273 '# Checked after the slow write; the rename after it takes at most about 2s, inside LOCK_STALE.' vs manifest.py:196-199 'age = time.time() - lock.stat().st_mtime ... if age <= LOCK_STALE: return' (lock mtime fixed at _acquire:241 owner write). Failing input: holder stalls 9s after acquire (fsync on a busy disk), check at age 9.0 passes, os.replace retries on PermissionError because an unlocked read_manifest reader has manifest.json open; at age 10.01 writer B steals, reads the old file, publishes its entry; A's replace then lands and B's entry is gone.

finding: The retry on deleting the temporary file is unproven: removing it leaves every test green
why: The only test of this line makes unlink fail on every attempt, so a mutant that replaces `_patient(temp.unlink, True)` with a single `temp.unlink(True)` passes all 119 tests (sampled probe on a scratch copy), and nothing shows a briefly locked temporary file is still removed.
fix: Add a case where Path.unlink raises PermissionError a few times for the .tmp file and then works, and assert the run folder holds only manifest.json afterwards.

finding: The '100 polls' test depends on real sleeps, so whether it gets past 100 polls depends on machine speed
why: It holds the lock for 2.5 s of wall time and relies on the real `time.sleep(0.02)` poll to make more than 100 attempts; this machine measured 123 mkdir attempts, so on a slower or loaded runner the count can drop below 101 and the guard against counting FileExistsError refusals passes without testing anything. It also adds 2.5 s to every run.
fix: Make it deterministic in the same way as `mkdir_refused`: raise FileExistsError more than 100 times while the lock exists, with sleep stubbed, then let mkdir succeed.
evidence: +    thread = release_later(lock, 2.5)  | measured: mkdir calls 123 in 2.5 s

finding: The mid-write theft test deletes the lock before the check, so the branch for a lock now held by another writer is never exercised
why: The thief writes its owner token and then runs `shutil.rmtree(lock)`, so `_owner` returns "" rather than the thief's token; a mutant that treats only a vanished lock as lost (`if _owner(lock) == "":`) passes all 119 tests, so the case where a stealer still holds the lock during the publish check is unproven.
fix: Add a case (or parametrize this one) where the thief's lock and owner file are still present at the publish check and released later, then assert the redo and that both changes land.
evidence: +        if len(writes) == 1:  # a thief takes the lock, publishes its own change and lets go ... +            shutil.rmtree(lock)  | mutant `if _owner(lock) == "":` -> 119 passed

finding: Likely: a temporary file that will not delete is now silently left in the run directory, not freed
why: The finally swallows the last OSError with no trace, so a stray manifest.json.<pid>.<hex>.tmp stays beside the manifest; nothing in the module sweeps it, and the new test checks only that no raw error escapes, never what is left on disk.
fix: Name the leftover (stderr line or swept by the next writer's publish), and assert its fate in test_a_temporary_file_that_will_not_delete_never_escapes_as_a_raw_error.
evidence: L280-284: `finally: try: _patient(temp.unlink, True) except OSError: pass`; commit 3bc3e23 subject says 'free a stuck temporary file without a raw error'

finding: Possible fragile test: the unreadable owner hits the publish check only because the publish check happens to be the first `_owner` call
why: `unreadable_once` returns None on whichever `_owner` call comes first; this currently works only because `_acquire` never calls `_owner` on an uncontested lock, so adding an ownership check in `_acquire` would quietly move the None away from the branch the test names.
fix: Return None only while the publish check runs, for example by stubbing `_owner` only after the fsync in the write has happened, or assert the call site that received None.
evidence: +        owners.append(None if not owners else real_owner(lock))
